reason: The supplied assembly shows each K step loading B at a 2048-byte stride while reading packed A at a 256-byte stride. That is a visible access pattern, not proof of a timing bottleneck. I rank the feasible, narrow ZA instruction-order change first; each tile retains its K order, though the full tolerance check is still required. Reusing scratch reservation and narrowing the fixed loop counter are also small source changes, with unverified benefit. Packing B one panel at a time could improve load locality, but adds repeated packing work; fused transpose avoids scratch traffic but repeats strided A loads and has higher correctness risk. The last two proposals request the same unavailable N=64 helper and wrapper layout, so they are both low priority and require host-side helper preparation. No instruction count or noisy score establishes a speedup.
